skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Backend development guidelines for Supabase Edge Functions, PostgreSQL, RLS, authentication, validation, email, payments, testing, and deployment patterns.
skill.summary: Guide backend teams through secure Supabase and TypeScript backend patterns.
skill.author: DojoCodingLabs

security_audit.summary: The static findings are overwhelmingly documentation-only matches, including Markdown backticks, template literals, relative imports, placeholder URLs, and environment-variable examples. No prompt injection or executable malware behavior was found, but one Sentry monitoring example recommends broad request data capture that could expose sensitive data.

remediation.suggestion: Disable request body and broad header capture by default. Only allow specific safe fields after data classification.
Replace values such as live-looking API keys, passwords, and tokens with clearly redacted placeholders.

remediation.issue: Mixed scaffold examples across backend stacks
remediation.suggestion: Label Supabase, Express, Prisma, and monitoring examples clearly so users do not copy incompatible patterns.

semantic_findings.description: The Sentry example enables local variable capture and request data capture for bodies, headers, IP addresses, query strings, URLs, and user identifiers. This can send sensitive application data to a third-party monitoring service if copied without narrower defaults.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited configuration explicitly enables broad request and user fields. The example also masks some data, so the risk is privacy exposure rather than malicious exfiltration.

content.value_statement: Backend teams need repeatable patterns for secure Supabase services. This skill provides practical guidance for Edge Functions, PostgreSQL, RLS, validation, testing, and deployment.
actual_capabilities: Explains Supabase Edge Function structure, request handling, CORS, authentication, and deployment commands.
Provides PostgreSQL schema, migration, indexing, and Row-Level Security policy examples.
Documents TypeScript validation, service, repository, controller, middleware, and error-handling patterns.
Shows integration patterns for Supabase Auth, Storage, Realtime, Resend, Stripe, and Sentry.
Includes local testing, CLI usage, and example workflows for backend feature delivery.
limitations: Examples are scaffold guidance and must be adapted before production use.
The skill does not inspect a live database, cloud project, or deployed Supabase configuration.
It cannot replace a security review of generated policies, secrets, or payment flows.
Some resource examples mix Supabase patterns with Node, Express, Prisma, and Sentry patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan a Supabase Feature
use_cases.description: Design tables, RLS policies, Edge Functions, validation, tests, and deployment steps for a new backend feature.

use_cases.title: Standardize Backend Patterns
use_cases.description: Create shared conventions for services, repositories, controllers, middleware, errors, and configuration management.

use_cases.title: Review Security Controls
use_cases.description: Check that authentication, RLS, input validation, secret handling, and monitoring patterns are included in backend work.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Edge Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple Supabase endpoint.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a Supabase Edge Function for [feature]. Include auth, Zod validation, RLS-aware database access, errors, and local testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design Schema and RLS
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate database planning for a feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design PostgreSQL tables and RLS policies for [domain]. Include indexes, migrations, ownership rules, and test cases.

prompt_templates.title: Add Integrations Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add [Stripe, Resend, Storage, or Sentry] to my backend. Show secret handling, failure modes, monitoring, and deployment checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Backend Implementation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing codebase.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my backend plan for [feature]. Identify missing auth, RLS, validation, configuration, testing, and observability controls.

output_examples.input: Plan a posts feature with authenticated create and public read access.
output: A table and migration outline for posts, comments, and ownership fields.
RLS policy guidance for published reads and owner-only writes.
An Edge Function checklist covering JWT verification, validation, error handling, and local tests.

output_examples.input: Review a Stripe webhook implementation for Supabase Edge Functions.
output: A review of signature verification, secret handling, idempotency, and event filtering.
Deployment notes for Supabase secrets and webhook environment variables.
Test scenarios for valid events, replayed events, and failed payment states.

output_examples.input: Create team conventions for backend service layers.
output: A recommended separation between controllers, services, repositories, middleware, and shared errors.
Guidance for validation boundaries and structured error responses.
Testing expectations for repositories, services, and authenticated routes.

best_practices: Adapt every scaffold example to your real schema, auth model, and deployment environment.
Verify JWTs, enforce RLS, validate input, and test policies before deploying functions.
Store secrets in managed environment configuration and avoid realistic secret values in examples.
anti_patterns: Copying examples into production without reviewing RLS, CORS, secrets, and error behavior.
Using service role keys for user-scoped operations that should rely on RLS.
Capturing request bodies, headers, or user data in monitoring tools without minimization rules.

faq.question: What stack does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Supabase Edge Functions, PostgreSQL, Row-Level Security, Supabase Auth, TypeScript, Resend, Stripe, and related backend patterns.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Supabase?
faq.answer: Yes, but you must adapt the examples. Some resources also show Express, Prisma, configuration, and monitoring patterns.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides scaffold guidance and examples. You must review security, secrets, RLS, tests, and deployment settings before production.

faq.question: Does it cover database security?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes RLS policies, ownership checks, migration examples, indexes, and testing approaches for database access.

faq.question: Does it handle payments and email?
faq.answer: It includes example patterns for Stripe payments, Stripe webhooks, and Resend transactional email integration.

faq.question: What should I review most carefully?
faq.answer: Review service role usage, secrets, webhook validation, CORS, monitoring data capture, and all RLS policies.
